reason: The young Sun interacting with the disk seems like a useful starting point for its temperature differences.
expectation: I expect the Sun to heat or illuminate the disk, though the precise result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust may advance the inner-disk goal, but I want to establish the Sun’s effect first.

effect: The result establishes that sunlight and accretion heat the inner disk, setting up the inner-orbit chemistry.
reaction: The distinction between sunlight and accretion heating is useful.
reason: Putting ice-mantled dust in hot inner orbits should show what happens to its water.
expectation: I expect the ice to evaporate or sublimate, leaving less volatile dust; the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This may develop the hot region further, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: The ice sublimated into vapor rather than disappearing, so I can now follow the water toward colder orbits.
reaction: The distinction between losing ice and losing water is useful.
reason: Moving the vapor into cold outer orbits seems relevant to storing ice beyond the snow line.
expectation: I expect the water vapor to freeze onto solids or form ice in the colder region, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This could advance the inner-disk goal, but I want to follow the water first.

effect: Water vapor can recondense after transport to colder orbits, providing another source of outer-disk ice.
reaction: Following the water through sublimation and recondensation is satisfying.
reason: Combining the recondensed ice with ice-mantled dust seems likely to advance the outer-disk ice goal.
expectation: I expect a collection of icy solids beyond the snow line, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This may advance the rocky inner-disk goal, but I want to finish following the ice first.

effect: The outer-disk ice goal is complete, so the remaining focus is the rocky inner disk.
reaction: It is useful to see inherited and reprocessed ice together.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the inner-disk goal.
expectation: I expect it to develop the hot inner region or its rocky material, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The hottest inner region vaporizes inherited grains, so rocky material must form from reprocessed vapor.
reaction: It is useful to see that inherited grains can be completely reprocessed.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may allow the vapor to cool.
expectation: I expect the vapor to lose heat and possibly condense into solids, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced high-temperature mineral grains, which can now be combined with rocky dust.
reaction: The contrast with ice condensation is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the rocky inner-disk mixture.
expectation: I expect a mixture of refractory grains and rock-forming dust, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The refractory grains and rocky dust formed a loose aggregate with mixed histories; further processing is needed for the remaining goal.
reaction: The reminder that the grains have different histories is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the inner-disk rocky mixture.
expectation: I expect the brief heating to melt or alter some of the aggregate's minerals, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Brief heating melted some solids into droplets; the heating mechanism remains unresolved.
reaction: Leaving the disputed mechanism open is a useful qualification.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may cool the molten droplets.
expectation: I expect the droplets to cool and solidify, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The molten droplets solidified into chondrules, preserving evidence of their heating and cooling.
reaction: The connection between particle textures and thermal history is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the rocky mixture.
expectation: I expect a mixture of chondrules and metal grains, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The stone-and-metal mixture completes the inner-disk goal, while making clear that ingredients alone do not make a planet.
reaction: The distinction between a mixture and a formed planet is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following water from sublimation to recondensation made the disk’s temperature differences concrete and showed that water is reprocessed, not simply lost.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of only-offered combinations toward the rocky mixture felt somewhat mechanical, even though the explanations were informative.

surprise.text: Chondrule textures can preserve evidence of rapid heating and cooling, even though the heating mechanism remains disputed.

arbitrary.text: Using open space to cool vapor and molten droplets felt somewhat abstract, although the cooling results had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue: tracing how these distinct icy and rocky materials become larger bodies seems interesting, despite the limited choices in the latter half.
